title: What Sign In does
fullTitle: Watch What Happens When You Click 'Sign In'

captions.text: Wrong password: 401. Right password: 200 and one cookie.
One implementation, not every sign-in system.
Browser · HTTPS · server · user database · session store.
Three objects: password, session id, authorisation decision.
Credentials travel inside the encrypted connection.
HTTPS protects transit, not a compromised endpoint. Illustrated, not executed.
Stored: a salted argon2id hash, not the password. One way, not reversible.
Observed: two hashes of the same password differ; both verify.
Success: regenerate. Pre-auth id destroyed, fresh id created.
Observed: old id replayed after login → 401.
Set-Cookie: sid=<opaque>; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/ — no Domain.
HttpOnly limits ordinary JS access. It does not stop every session attack.
GET /me + cookie → store lookup → 200, u_alice.
The cookie identifies a session. It carries no permission.
Two checks: session valid? then permitted?
Observed: no cookie 401 · member 403 · admin 200.
POST /logout with CSRF token: record destroyed, cookie expired.
Observed: GET /logout 405 · no token 403 · replay after logout 401.
The cookie identifies a session. The server enforces access.
One implementation. Memory store not for production. TLS leg illustrated.
